classification.difficultyReason: Requires intersecting two parameter-dependent open intervals and expressing their intersection using its centre and radius.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch the possible values of $x$ on a number line.

answer.worked:
The first inequality gives
$$\begin{align*}-a&<x-a<a\\0&<x<2a.\end{align*}$$
The second gives
$$\begin{align*}-a&<x-2a<a\\a&<x<3a.\end{align*}$$
Both hold on their intersection, $a<x<2a$. Use open endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 77(a); solution reference teacher PDF 14, printed page 318
spec.description: Open interval from a to 2a on a number line with 0 retained to its left.
spec.mathematics: (0,2a) intersected with (a,3a) is (a,2a), since a > 0. Positions 0, a and 2a retain their proportional spacing.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; the student must draw the number line without a supplied scaffold.
spec.shadingDecision: No area shading. White-filled endpoint markers indicate excluded endpoints.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find $c$ and $r$ in terms of $a$ such that $|x-c|<r$.

answer.short:
$c=\frac{3a}{2}$, $r=\frac a2$.

Use the midpoint and half-length of $(a,2a)$.
answer.worked:
The interval $a<x<2a$ has centre $c$ and radius $r$:
$$\begin{align*}c&=\frac{a+2a}{2}\\c&=\frac{3a}{2}\\r&=\frac{2a-a}{2}\\r&=\frac a2.\end{align*}$$
Thus the same interval is $\left|x-\frac{3a}{2}\right|<\frac a2$.
